name: voice
description: Voice-mode and dictation instructions (how the assistant should treat spoken input and answer when you are talking, not typing) + Claude Code voice dictation enabled for this project.

rules.dictation:
---
description: How to interpret dictated (voice) input
---
# Dictation instructions

Some prompts arrive through voice dictation. Treat them as spoken language, not as literal text:
- Ignore filler words (um, uh, like, you know) and self-corrections; keep the final intent.
- Infer punctuation and casing. Spoken "new line"/"new paragraph" mean line breaks; "open paren ... close paren" mean brackets; "quote ... end quote" mean quotation marks.
- Spoken identifiers: "camel case user name" -> `userName`, "snake case max retries" -> `max_retries`, "dot env" -> `.env`, "dash dash force" -> `--force`, "slash" -> `/`.
- Spoken numbers become digits; "version three point twelve" -> `3.12`.
- Homophones in a coding context: "write" vs "right", "two"/"to", "four"/"for" - pick the code-meaningful one and say which you assumed.
- If a dictated instruction would run a command, delete files, or touch git history, repeat it back in one line and wait for an explicit yes.
- When a transcription is ambiguous, ask a single short clarifying question instead of guessing.
rules.voice-mode:
---
description: How to respond while the user is in voice mode
---
# Voice-mode instructions

When the user is interacting by voice (voice mode on, or they say so):
- Answer first in one or two spoken-friendly sentences; details after, in short bullets.
- Do not read long code aloud: write the code to a file or the chat, then say what it does and where it is.
- Avoid tables, ASCII art, long paths and hex strings in the spoken part; say "I put the path in the chat".
- Confirm before destructive or irreversible actions with a yes/no question.
- Use the project's words (file names, feature names) exactly as the user says them; do not rename things.
- Keep status updates to one line while working; offer the next step at the end.

notes: Claude Code: toggle with /voice (modes hold | tap | off); the push-to-talk key is rebindable in ~/.claude/keybindings.json (yours to edit, not aisb's). Dictation language follows the `language` setting.

Antigravity CLI: /voice or F5. Cursor: Voice Mode in Settings > Voice (submit keywords). These tools have no 'dictation instruction' setting, so the rules above are delivered as project instructions instead.
